advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a table-driven test asserting `_UPSTREAM_RE.search(...)` returns None for the lookalike hosts (https://notpandoc.org, https://pandoc.org.evil.com, github.com/jgm/pandoc-extras) and matches for the real https:// upstream URLs.
evidence: Sole use: `assert _UPSTREAM_RE.search(text)` at line 58, where `text` is the real NOTICE which matches the accept path.
Real NOTICE contains `Upstream:   https://pandoc.org  (source: https://github.com/jgm/pandoc)` (NOTICE:17), so only the positive/accept branch is exercised.

ABSENCE: no test asserts `_UPSTREAM_RE.search('https://notpandoc.org') is None`, `...('https://pandoc.org.evil.com') is None`, or `...('https://github.com/jgm/pandoc-extras') is None`. A regression that swaps `(?![\w.-])` for `\b` (which the commit message says would wrongly accept pandoc.org.evil.com) would leave the existing test green — the fix's intent is unguarded.
advisory.finding: The new _UPSTREAM_RE anchoring exists specifically to reject lookalike upstream hosts (prefix https://notpandoc.org, suffix https://pandoc.org.evil.com, sibling github.com/jgm/pandoc-extras), but no test asserts those strings FAIL the regex — the only assertion runs the regex against the real NOTICE, exercising only the accept path.
scenarios: Someone loosens the negative lookaheads or reverts to substring containment; the real-NOTICE assertion still passes, so the CodeQL-alert-#88 fix silently regresses.
